How we help

From first search to front door.

Buying a home shouldn’t feel like being sold to. Here’s how we make it simple.

  1. 01

    Tell us what matters

    Budget, configuration, location and when you want to move in. Five minutes, no obligation.

  2. 02

    Get a real shortlist

    Projects that genuinely fit — compared side by side on plans, pricing, amenities and timelines.

  3. 03

    Visit with confidence

    We plan the site visits and tell you exactly what to look for and what to ask the builder.

  4. 04

    Close and move in

    Negotiation, booking and paperwork — we stay with you until the keys are in your hand.

Why AcreInfotech

Advice that’s on your side of the table.

We work for you, not the builder.

Most property platforms are built to close a lead. We’re built to help you make one of the biggest decisions of your life well — which sometimes means telling you to walk away.

How we work

Complete property information

Floor plans, configurations, amenities, location and registration details — all in one place.

Honest comparisons

See projects side by side on the same basis — area, price and possession — not brochure claims.

Registered projects only

Every project we list carries its UP-RERA registration number, so you can check it yourself.

Through to handover

Site visits, negotiation and paperwork — we’re with you until you move in.

Buyer questions

Good questions to ask before you buy.

Can’t find yours? Ask us directly.

How do I know a project is registered?

Every project we list carries its UP-RERA registration number on its page. You can look that number up yourself on the UP-RERA portal before you commit to anything.

What's the difference between carpet, built-up and super area?

Carpet area is the usable floor inside your walls. Built-up adds the walls and balconies. Super area also adds your share of lobbies, lifts and common spaces — which is why it's always the biggest number on a brochure. Compare projects on the same basis.

What does the possession date actually mean?

It's the date by which the builder has declared the home will be handed over. Look at the project's construction progress and the builder's past delivery record, not just the date itself.

How do I get started?

Browse the projects here, or tell us your budget, preferred location and configuration through the contact page — we'll come back with a shortlist that fits.

Tell us what you’re looking for and we’ll come back with a shortlist that actually fits.
